name: Dark Lilac
lede: Dark Lilac is a deeper, more saturated [[lilac]], a purple the ISCC-NBS system classes as a moderate purple.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this exact position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark lilac" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is moderate purple, about 7 CIEDE2000 units from this swatch, and the closest Munsell reading is near 6.5P in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[viola]], [[orchid-purple]] and [[faded-purple]], at 3.2, 3.6 and 3.7 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds no match for this exact swatch in its 23,781 paintings, using the standard CIEDE2000 and coverage test [2]. That is a statement about this particular shade, not about purple in general: lighter and darker purples both appear elsewhere in the archive [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so an absence here is a gap in what survives on canvas, not a claim that the color was never used [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
